newsitem.title: UK: BT and Viag start proceedings against Global One.
newsitem.headline: BT and Viag start proceedings against Global One.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc on Wednesday said it and its German partner Viag launched legal proceedings in Germany against Global One to ensure fair competition in national telecom markets.

BT and Viag want to stop Global One, a venture between Sprint Corp from the U.S., France Telecom and Deutsche Telekom, from carrying on its businesses as long as rivals have hardly any choice in finding alternative network suppliers.
Global One was only given EU clearance on condition that its competitors can obtain supplies from at least two operators in addition to Deutsche Telekom and France Telecom, BT said.
But licences for such operators have yet to be granted in France and Germany, it added.
A BT spokesman told Reuters the legal proceedings were also aimed at speeding up the issue of sufficient licences by the relevant authorities.

Three licences were awarded in Germany on Tuesday, but two of these were purely local ones, while only one was an international licence. At least one other international licence was needed, the spokesman said.

The legal proceedings come nearly a week after industry sources said that Viag Intercom, the joint venture between Viag and BT, and five other firms filed a complaint in Brussels over the licence issue.

In their Brussels complaint, the six firms said that, while Deutsche Telekom will grant big discounts to its customers, it is charging rivals inflated prices for leased-lines, preventing them from offering competitive prices.
The licence row comes just weeks before Deutsche Telekom's international share listing.

BT, meanwhile, said it and Viag Interkom expect the necessary licences will be granted in the near future, adding this "...is essential for the attainment of fair and effective competition in Europe."
